definition.def: If a person or living thing survives in a dangerous situation such as an accident or an illness, they do not die.
examples: They battled to survive in icy seas for over four hours. [VERB]
Those organisms that are most suited to the environment will survive. [VERB]
Drugs that dissolve blood clots can help people survive heart attacks. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If you survive in difficult circumstances, you manage to live or continue in spite of them and do not let them affect you very much.
examples: On my first day here I thought, 'Ooh, how will I survive?' [VERB]
...people who are struggling to survive without jobs. [VERB]
Where once she had been totally self-sufficient, she now had to survive on income support. [VERB on noun]
...a man who had survived his share of boardroom coups. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If something survives, it continues to exist even after being in a dangerous situation or existing for a long time.
examples: When the market economy is introduced, many factories will not survive. [VERB]
The chances of a planet surviving a supernova always looked terribly slim. [VERB noun]
...surviving examples of 19th-century architecture in the Mid-West. [VERB-ing]

definition.def: If you survive someone, you continue to live after they have died.
examples: Most women will survive their spouses. [VERB noun]
She is survived by two daughters from her first marriage. [VERB noun]
